extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: SWE-Gym is an environment for training software engineering agents. It contains 2,438 real-world task instances, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors used SEART GitHub search to filter Python repositories based on specific criteria (creation date, stars, lines of code, PRs, contributors). They then used SWE-Bench's extraction script to convert these repositories into task instances, semi-automatically collected versions, manually configured dependencies, and validated the instances using execution-based scripts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real-world software engineering tasks sourced from pull requests in popular Python repositories, consisting of natural language issue descriptions, repository snapshots, and unit tests.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset exhibits a skewed, long-tail distribution across repositories, with a significant overrepresentation of certain codebases like pandas.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended to be used as a training environment for software engineering agents and verifier models.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was constructed by filtering Python repositories created before July 1, 2022, with over 500 stars, at least 300 lines of code, over 500 pull requests, and 100 contributors. Repositories were converted into task instances using an extraction script. For the Lite subset, tasks were further filtered to exclude those requiring edits to multiple files, having poorly described problem statements, overly complex ground-truth diffs, or tests focused on error message validation.

name.evidence: We present SWE-Gym, the first environment for training software engineering (SWE) agents.

description.evidence: SWE-Gym contains 2,438 real-world task instances, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: SWE-Gym comprises 2,438 real-world software engineering tasks sourced from pull requests in 11 popular Python repositories... each corresponding to a GitHub issue including the natural language description of the issue, a snapshot of the repository in which the issue was created, and a set of unit tests.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Fig. 2 illustrates that the task distribution across repositories exhibits a long-tail pattern. Notably, tasks associated with pandas comprise nearly one-third of the total, whereas tasks related to bokeh represent a mere one percent.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: In this paper, we introduce SWE-Gym, the first training environment that addresses critical gaps in enabling scalable learning for software engineering agents. [...] SWE-Gym enables both agent and verifier models to achieve significant improvements in resolving complex software tasks.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: we select Python repositories that were created before July 1, 2022 and have more than 500 stars, with at least 300 lines of code, more than 500 pull requests (PRs) and 100 contributors.
